notable_features.text: German is notable for its flexible word order, which lacks a single dominant pattern and instead relies on case marking and verb position rules to convey grammatical relationships. It also has a rich verbal system that marks seven distinct tense/aspect categories, and a relatively large phoneme inventory of 41 sounds compared to many other languages. As a West Germanic language, it serves as an official or recognized language across a wide range of European countries and communities beyond Germany itself.
